newsitem.title: USA: April U.S. light vehicle sales fall 3.8 percent.
newsitem.headline: April U.S. light vehicle sales fall 3.8 percent.

text.p: U.S. car and light truck sales during the month of April totaled 1,279,751 units with all automakers reporting. The April sales were 3.8 percent less than the 1,330,136 units sold a year earlier.

The seasonally adjusted annual sales rate for the month was 14.33 million units, down from 15.09 million units a year earlier, and 15.83 million units for the month of March. The rate is calculated with seasonal factors supplied by the U.S. Commerce Department.
Automakers sold 579,515 North American-built cars in the United States in April, down 10.6 percent from a year ago.
The seasonally adjusted annual rate for domestic cars was 6.48 million units, compared with 7.33 million in April 1996 and 7.09 million in March.

Automakers sold 536,972 domestic trucks in the United States during April, up 0.4 percent from a year earlier. The seasonally adjusted annual sales rate for domestic trucks was 5.87 million units, compared with 5.96 million a year earlier and 6.57 million in March.

Imported car sales totaled 121,735 units, up 8.1 percent from a year ago, with a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 1.46 million units. Imported truck sales rose 20.4 percent to 41,529 units for an annual rate of 530,000 units.
